verses.zh: 我的仆人雅各，我所拣选的以色列啊，现在你当听。
verses.en: “Now, listen, Jacob my servant,Israel whom I have chosen!”

verses.zh: 造作你，又从你出胎造就你，并要帮助你的耶和华如此说：我的仆人雅各，我所拣选的耶书仑哪，不要害怕！
verses.en: This is what the Lord, the one who made you, says—the one who formed you in the womb and helps you:“Don’t be afraid, my servant Jacob,Jeshurun,[NOTE:1] whom I have chosen.
notes: Jeshurun is a poetic name for Israel; it occurs here and in Deut 32:15; 33:5, 26.

verses.zh: 因为我要将水浇灌口渴的人，将河浇灌干旱之地。我要将我的灵浇灌你的后裔，将我的福浇灌你的子孙。
verses.en: For I will pour water on the parched ground[NOTE:1] and cause streams to flow[NOTE:2] on the dry land.I will pour my Spirit on your offspringand my blessing on your children.
notes: Heb “the thirsty.” Parallelism suggests that dry ground is in view (see “dry land” in the next line.)
Heb “and streams”; KJV “floods.” The verb “cause…to flow” is supplied in the second line for clarity and for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 他们要发生在草中，像溪水旁的柳树。
verses.en: They will sprout up like a tree in the grass,[NOTE:1] like poplars beside channels of water.
notes: The Hebrew term בֵין (ven) is usually taken as a preposition, in which case one might translate, “among the grass.” But בֵין is probably the name of a tree (cf. C. R. North, Second Isaiah, 133). If one alters the preposition bet (בְּ) to kaf (כְּ), one can then read, “like a binu-tree.” (The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa supports this reading.) This forms a nice parallel to “like poplars” in the next line. חָצִיר (khatsir) is functioning as an adverbial accusative of location.

verses.zh: 这个要说：我是属耶和华的；那个要以雅各的名自称；又一个要亲手写：归耶和华的（或译：在手上写归耶和华），并自称为以色列。
verses.en: One will say, ‘I belong to the Lord,’and another will use[NOTE:1] the name ‘Jacob.’One will write on his hand, ‘The Lord’s,’and use the name ‘Israel.’”[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew text has a Qal verb form, “and another will call by the name of Jacob.” With support from Symmachus (an ancient Greek textual witness), some read the Niphal, “and another will be called by the name of Jacob.”

Heb “and by the name of Israel he will title.” Some, with support from several ancient versions, prefer to change the Piel (active) verb form to a Pual (passive), “and he will be titled by the name of Israel.”

verses.zh: 耶和华―以色列的君，以色列的救赎主―万军之耶和华如此说：我是首先的，我是末后的；除我以外再没有真神。
verses.en: This is what the Lord, Israel’s King, says,their Protector,[NOTE:1] the Lord of Heaven’s Armies:“I am the first and I am the last,there is no God but me.
notes: Heb “his kinsman redeemer.” See the note at 41:14.

verses.zh: 自从我设立古时的民，谁能像我宣告，并且指明，又为自己陈说呢？让他将未来的事和必成的事说明。
verses.en: Who is like me? Let him make his claim![NOTE:1] Let him announce it and explain it to me—since I established an ancient people[NOTE:2]— let them announce future events.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “let him call” or “let him proclaim” (so NASB, NIV, NRSV); NAB “Let him stand up and speak.”

The Hebrew text reads, “from (the time) I established an ancient people, and the coming things.” Various emendations have been proposed. One of the options assumes the reading מַשְׁמִיעִים מֵעוֹלָם אוֹתִיּוֹת (mashmiʿim meʿolam ʾotiyyot); This literally reads “the ones causing to hear from antiquity coming things,” but more idiomatically would read “as for those who predict from antiquity what will happen” (cf. NAB, NEB, REB). The emendation directs the attention of the reader to those who claim to be able to predict the future, challenging them to actually do what they claim they can do. The MT presents Yahweh as an example to whom these alleged “predictors of the future” can compare themselves. Since the ancient versions are unanimous in their support of the MT, the emendations should be set aside.
Heb and those things which are coming let them declare for themselves.”

verses.zh: 你们不要恐惧，也不要害怕。我岂不是从上古就说明指示你们吗？并且你们是我的见证！除我以外，岂有真神吗？诚然没有磐石，我不知道一个！
verses.en: Don’t panic! Don’t be afraid![NOTE:1] Did I not tell you beforehand and decree it?You are my witnesses! Is there any God but me?There is no other sheltering rock;[NOTE:2] I know of none.
notes: BDB 923 s.v. רָהָה derives this verb from an otherwise unattested root, while HALOT 403 s.v. יָרָה defines it as “be stupefied” on the basis of an Arabic cognate. The form likely needs to be emended to תיראו, the reading attested in the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa.
Heb “rock” or “rocky cliff,” a title that depicts God as a protective refuge in his role as sovereign king; thus the translation “sheltering rock.”

verses.zh: 制造雕刻偶像的尽都虚空；他们所喜悦的都无益处；他们的见证无所看见，无所知晓，他们便觉羞愧。
verses.en: All who form idols are nothing;the things in which they delight are worthless.Their witnesses cannot see;they recognize nothing, so they are put to shame.

verses.zh: 谁制造神像，铸造无益的偶像？
verses.en: Who forms a god and casts an idolthat will prove worthless?[NOTE:1]
notes: The rhetorical question is sarcastic. The sense is, “Who is foolish enough…?”

verses.zh: 看哪，他的同伴都必羞愧。工匠也不过是人，任他们聚会，任他们站立，都必惧怕，一同羞愧。
verses.en: Look, all his associates[NOTE:1] will be put to shame;the craftsmen are mere humans.[NOTE:2] Let them all assemble and take their stand.They will panic and be put to shame.
notes: The pronoun “his” probably refers to the one who forms/casts an idol (v. 10), in which case it refers to the craftsman’s associates in the idol-manufacturing guild.
The point seems to be this: if the idols are the mere products of human hands, then those who trust in them will be disappointed, for man-made gods are incapable of helping their “creators.”

verses.zh: 铁匠把铁在火炭中烧热，用锤打铁器，用他有力的膀臂锤成；他饥饿而无力，不喝水而发倦。
verses.en: A blacksmith works with his tool[NOTE:1] and forges metal over the coals.He forms it[NOTE:2] with hammers;he makes it with his strong arm.He gets hungry and loses his energy;[NOTE:3] he drinks no water and gets tired.
notes: The noun מַעֲצָד (maʿatsad), which refers to some type of tool used for cutting, occurs only here and in Jer 10:3. See HALOT 615 s.v. מַעֲצָד.

Some English versions take the pronoun “it” to refer to an idol being fashioned by the blacksmith (cf. NIV, NCV, CEV). NLT understands the referent to be “a sharp tool,” which is then used by the carpenter in the following verse to carve an idol from wood.
Heb “and there is no strength”; NASB “his strength fails.”

verses.zh: 木匠拉线，用笔划出样子，用刨子刨成形状，用圆尺划了模样，仿照人的体态，做成人形，好住在房屋中。
verses.en: A carpenter takes measurements;[NOTE:1] he marks out an outline of its form;[NOTE:2] he scrapes[NOTE:3] it with chiselsand marks it with a compass.He patterns it after the human form,[NOTE:4] like a well-built human being,and puts it in a shrine.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “stretches out a line” (ASV similar); NIV “measures with a line.”

Heb “he makes an outline with the [?].” The noun שֶׂרֶד (shered) occurs only here; it apparently refers to some type of tool or marker. Cf. KJV “with a line”; ASV “with a pencil”; NAB, NRSV “with a stylus”; NASB “with red chalk”; NIV “with a marker.”
Heb “works” (so NASB) or “fashions” (so NRSV); NIV “he roughs it out.”
Heb “he makes it like the pattern of a man”; NAB “like a man in appearance.”
Heb “like the glory of man to sit [in] a house”; NIV “that it may dwell in a shrine.”

verses.zh: 他砍伐香柏树，又取柞（或译：青桐）树和橡树，在树林中选定了一棵。他栽种松树，得雨长养。
verses.en: He cuts down cedarsand acquires a cypress[NOTE:1] or an oak.He gets[NOTE:2] trees from the forest;he plants a cedar[NOTE:3] and the rain makes it grow.
notes: It is not certain what type of tree this otherwise unattested noun refers to. Cf. ASV “a holm-tree” (NRSV similar).
Heb “strengthens for himself,” i.e., “secures for himself” (see BDB 55 s.v. אָמֵץ Pi.2).

Some prefer to emend אֹרֶן (ʾoren) to אֶרֶז (ʾerez, “cedar”), but the otherwise unattested noun appears to have an Akkadian cognate, meaning “cedar.” See H. R. Cohen, Biblical Hapax Legomena (SBLDS), 44-45. HALOT 90 s.v. I אֹרֶן offers the meaning “laurel.”

verses.zh: 这树，人可用以烧火；他自己取些烤火，又烧着烤饼，而且做神像跪拜，做雕刻的偶像向它叩拜。
verses.en: A man uses it to make a fire;[NOTE:1] he takes some of it and warms himself.Yes, he kindles a fire and bakes bread.Then he makes a god and worships it;he makes an idol and bows down to it.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and it becomes burning [i.e., firewood] for a man”; NAB “to serve man for fuel.”
Or perhaps, “them.”

verses.zh: 他把一分烧在火中，把一分烤肉吃饱。自己烤火说：「啊哈，我暖和了，我见火了。」
verses.en: Half of it he burns in the fire—over that half he cooks[NOTE:1] meat;he roasts a meal and fills himself.Yes, he warms himself and says,‘Ah! I am warm as I look at the fire.’
notes: Heb “eats” (so NASB); NAB, NRSV “roasts.”

verses.zh: 他用剩下的做了一神，就是雕刻的偶像。他向这偶像俯伏叩拜，祷告它说：「求你拯救我，因你是我的神。」
verses.en: With the rest of it he makes a god, his idol;he bows down to it and worships it.He prays to it, saying,‘Rescue me, for you are my god!’

verses.zh: 他们不知道，也不思想；因为耶和华闭住他们的眼，不能看见，塞住他们的心，不能明白。
verses.en: They do not comprehend or understand,for their eyes are blind and cannot see;their minds do not discern.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “for their eyes are smeared over so they cannot see, so their heart cannot be wise.”

verses.zh: 谁心里也不醒悟，也没有知识，没有聪明，能说：「我曾拿一分在火中烧了，在炭火上烤过饼；我也烤过肉吃。这剩下的，我岂要作可憎的物吗？我岂可向木墩子叩拜呢？」
verses.en: No one thinks to himself,nor do they comprehend or understand and say to themselves:‘I burned half of it in the fire—yes, I baked bread over the coals;I roasted meat and ate it.With the rest of it should I make a disgusting idol?Should I bow down to dry wood?’[NOTE:1]
notes: There is no formal interrogative sign here, but the context seems to indicate these are rhetorical questions. See GKC 473 §150.a.

verses.zh: 他以灰为食，心中昏迷，使他偏邪，他不能自救，也不能说：「我右手中岂不是有虚谎吗？」
verses.en: He feeds on ashes;[NOTE:1] his deceived mind misleads him.He cannot rescue himself,nor does he say, ‘Is this not a false god I hold in my right hand?’[NOTE:2]
notes: Or perhaps, “he eats on an ash heap.”
Heb “Is it not a lie in my right hand?”

verses.zh: 雅各，以色列啊，你是我的仆人，要记念这些事。以色列啊，你是我的仆人，我造就你必不忘记你。
verses.en: Remember these things, O Jacob,O Israel, for you are my servant.I formed you to be my servant;O Israel, I will not forget you![NOTE:1]
notes: The verb in the Hebrew text is a Niphal imperfect with a pronominal suffix. Although the Niphal ordinarily has the passive sense, it can have a reflexive nuance as well (see above translation). Some have suggested an emendation to a Qal form: “Do not forget me” (all the ancient versions, NEB, REB; see GKC 369 §117.x). “Do not forget me” would make a good parallel with “remember these things” in the first line. Since the MT is the harder reading and fits with Israel’s complaint that God had forgotten her (Isa 40:27), the MT reading should be retained (NASB, NKJV, NRSV, ESV, HCSB). The passive has been rendered as an active in the translation in keeping with contemporary English style (so also NIV, NCV, TEV, NLT).

verses.zh: 我涂抹了你的过犯，像厚云消散；我涂抹了你的罪恶，如薄云灭没。你当归向我，因我救赎了你。
verses.en: I remove the guilt of your rebellious deeds as if they were a cloud,the guilt of your sins as if they were a cloud.[NOTE:1] Come back to me, for I protect[NOTE:2] you.”
notes: Heb “I blot out like a cloud your rebellious deeds, and like a cloud your sins.” “Rebellious deeds” and “sins” stand by metonymy for the guilt they produce. Both עָב (ʿav) and עָנָן (ʿanan) refer to the clouds in the sky. It is tempting for stylistic purposes to translate the second with “fog” or “mist” (cf. NAB, NRSV “cloud…mist”; NIV “cloud…morning mist”; NLT “morning mists…clouds”), but this distinction between the synonyms is unwarranted here. The point of the simile seems to be this: The Lord forgives their sins, causing them to vanish just as clouds disappear from the sky (see Job 7:9; 30:15).
Heb “redeem.” See the note at 41:14.

verses.zh: 诸天哪，应当歌唱，因为耶和华做成这事。地的深处啊，应当欢呼；众山应当发声歌唱；树林和其中所有的树都当如此！因为耶和华救赎了雅各，并要因以色列荣耀自己。
verses.en: Shout for joy, O sky, for the Lord intervenes;[NOTE:1] shout out, you subterranean regions[NOTE:2] of the earth.O mountains, give a joyful shout;you too, O forest and all your trees![NOTE:3] For the Lord protects[NOTE:4] Jacob;he reveals his splendor through Israel.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “acts”; NASB, NRSV “has done it”; NLT “has done this wondrous thing.”
Heb “lower regions.” This refers to Sheol and forms a merism with “sky” in the previous line. See Pss 63:9; 71:20.
Heb “O forest and all the trees in it”; NASB, NRSV “and every tree in it.”
Heb “redeems.” See the note at 41:14.
That is, by delivering Israel. Cf. NCV “showed his glory when he saved Israel”; TEV “has shown his greatness by saving his people Israel.”

verses.zh: 从你出胎，造就你的救赎主―耶和华如此说：我―耶和华是创造万物的，是独自铺张诸天、铺开大地的。谁与我同在呢？
verses.en: This is what the Lord, your Protector,[NOTE:1] says,the one who formed you in the womb:“I am the Lord, who made everything,who alone stretched out the sky,who fashioned the earth all by myself,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “your redeemer.” See the note at 41:14.
The consonantal text (Kethib) has “Who [was] with me?” The marginal reading (Qere) is “from with me,” i.e., “by myself.” See BDB 87 s.v. II אֵת 4.c.

verses.zh: 使说假话的兆头失效，使占卜的癫狂，使智慧人退后，使他的知识变为愚拙；
verses.en: who frustrates the omens of the empty talkers[NOTE:1] and humiliates[NOTE:2] the omen readers,who overturns the counsel of the wise men[NOTE:3] and makes their advice[NOTE:4] seem foolish,
notes: The Hebrew text has בַּדִּים (baddim), perhaps meaning “empty talkers” (BDB 95 s.v. III בַּד). In the four other occurrences of this word (Job 11:3; Isa 16:6; Jer 48:30; 50:36) the context does not make the meaning of the term very clear. Its primary point appears to be that the words spoken are meaningless or false. In light of its parallelism with “omen readers,” some have proposed an emendation to בָּרִים (barim, “seers”). The Mesopotamian baru-priests were divination specialists who played an important role in court life. See R. Wilson, Prophecy and Society in Ancient Israel, 93-98. Rather than supporting an emendation, J. N. Oswalt (Isaiah [NICOT], 2:189, n. 79) suggests that Isaiah used בַּדִּים purposively as a derisive wordplay on the Akkadian word baru (in light of the close similarity of the d and r consonants).
Or “makes fools of” (NIV, NRSV); NAB and NASB both similar.
Heb “who turns back the wise” (so NRSV); NIV “overthrows the learning of the wise”; TEV “The words of the wise I refute.”
Heb “their knowledge” (so KJV, NAB, NASB, NRSV).

verses.zh: 使我仆人的话语立定，我使者的谋算成就。论到耶路撒冷说：必有人居住；论到犹大的城邑说：必被建造，其中的荒场我也必兴起。
verses.en: who fulfills the oracles of his prophetic servants[NOTE:1] and brings to pass the announcements[NOTE:2] of his messengers,who says about Jerusalem,[NOTE:3] ‘She will be inhabited,’and about the towns of Judah, ‘They will be rebuilt,her ruins I will raise up,’
notes: Heb “the word of his servant.” The following context indicates that the Lord’s prophets are in view.
Heb “counsel.” The Hebrew term עֵצָה (ʿetsah) probably refers here to the divine plan as announced by the prophets. See HALOT 867 s.v. I עֵצָה.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 对深渊说：你干了吧！我也要使你的江河干涸。
verses.en: who says to the deep sea, ‘Be dry!I will dry up your sea currents,’

verses.zh: 论塞鲁士说：他是我的牧人，必成就我所喜悦的，必下令建造耶路撒冷，发命立稳圣殿的根基。
verses.en: who commissions[NOTE:1] Cyrus, the one I appointed as shepherd[NOTE:2] to carry out all my wishes[NOTE:3] and to decree concerning Jerusalem, ‘She will be rebuilt,’and concerning the temple, ‘It will be reconstructed.’[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “says to.” It is possible that the sentence is not completed, as the description of Cyrus and his God-given role is developed in the rest of the verse. 45:1 picks up where 44:28a leaves off with the Lord’s actual words to Cyrus finally being quoted in 45:2.
Heb “my shepherd.” The shepherd motif is sometimes applied, as here, to a royal figure who is responsible for the well-being of the people whom he rules.
Heb “that he might bring to completion all my desire.”

Heb “and [concerning the] temple, you will be founded.” The preposition -לְ (le) is understood by ellipsis at the beginning of the second line. The verb תִּוָּסֵד (tivvased, “you will be founded”) is second masculine singular and is probably addressed to the personified temple (הֵיכָל [hekhal, “temple”] is masculine).

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 44:1-5

1"But now listen, O Jacob, My servant,

And Israel, whom I have chosen:

2Thus says the Lord who made you

And formed you from the womb, who will help you,

'Do not fear, O Jacob My servant;

And you Jeshurun whom I have chosen.

3For I will pour out water on the thirsty land

And streams on the dry ground;

I will pour out My Spirit on your offspring

And My blessing on your descendants;

4And they will spring up among the grass

Like poplars by streams of water.'

5This one will say, 'I am the Lord's';

And that one will call on the name of Jacob;

And another will write on his hand, 'Belonging to the Lord,'

And will name Israel's name with honor."

44:1 "listen" This is an IMPERATIVE (BDB 1033, KB 1570) which characterizes
many oracles in Isaiah (cf. Isa. 1:2,10; 6:8,9,10; 7:13; 28:14; 32:9; 33:13; 34:1; 36:13; 39:5; 42:18; 46:3,12; 47:8;
48:1,12,14, 16; 51:1,7,21; 55:2,3; 59:1; 66:5).

This word means "to hear so as to perform" (cf. James 1:22-25). It became the name (the Shema)
of the famous Jewish prayer in Deut. 6:4-5.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR

▣ "O Jacob, My servant" Notice the parellelism between lines 1 and 2. YHWH is addressing corporate Israel.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT

▣ "whom I have chosen" YHWH

- chose Israel, Isa. 44:1,2

- made Israel, Isa. 44:2

- formed Israel, Isa. 44:2 (cf. Isa. 27:11; 37:26; 43:1,7,21; 44:2,21-24; 45:11)

- helped Israel, Isa. 44:2

SPECIAL TOPIC: HE CHOSE US

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

44:2 Notice the parallelism between lines 1 and 2.

- "made you" ‒ BDB 793, KB 889, Qal PARTICIPLE, line 1, cf. Isa. 17:7

- "formed you" ‒ BDB 427, KB 428, Qal PARTICIPLE, line 2, cf. Gen. 2:7,8 (see #3 above)

There are several Hebrew words used to describe YHWH's creative acts.

▣ "Do not fear" This phrase (BDB 431, KB 432, Qal IMPERFECT used
in a JUSSIVE sense) is used often in chapters 40-66 (cf. Isa. 40:9; 41:10,13,14; 43:1,5; 44:3;
51:7; 54:4,14; 57:11). They were not to fear because

- they were God's people

- He was with them

- their punishment was over

- He would provide all they needed

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

▣ "Jeshurun" This (BDB 449) was a rare title for Israel meaning "the upright one"
(cf. Deut. 32:15; 33:5,26). It is parallel to "O Jacob My servant."

44:3 "I will pour" This VERB (BDB 427, KB 428, Qal IMPERFECT)
is often used in connection with anointings or sacrifices. In this verse it is repeated twice.

- once for the miraculous water of abundance

- once for the Spirit (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE)

- Isa. 32:15, different word (BDB 788)

- Joel 2:28, different word (BDB 1049)

YHWH is the source of blessings and for desert people water was the symbol of life and abundance (cf. Isa. 44:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS/SEA, I. A. #4

▣ "on your offspring" Blessings, like curses, moved through families (cf. Deut. 5:9-10; 7:9).

These future generations will know who they are in YHWH, i.e. if their parents teach them (cf. Deut. 4:9,10; 6:7,20-25; 11:19; 32:46), rejoice in it (Isa. 44:5), and live it!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

44:5 The textual question is to whom this verse refers.

- proud descendants of Abraham (v. 2)

- foreigners who claim and extol Israel's God (cf. v. 5; 56:3-6)

The VERB "call" (BDB 894, KB 1128, Qal VERB) is translated

- PASSIVE in the Aramaic Targums, "shall be called"

- REFLEXIVE (Niphal) in the LXX and the Peshitta, "shall call himself"

- ACTIVE in the Hebrew, "shall call on" (i.e. act of worship; see SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON HIS NAME)

It seems to me from the context of the parallelism of lines 2 and 3 that it is talking about foreigners
(see UBS Text Project, p. 116). If so, then this is one of those texts that assures non-Jews of access to the one true
God (cf. 1 Kgs. 8:41-43)! Not only is the servant a light to the nations (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 12:4-5; 25:6-9; 42:6-12; 45:22-23;
49:5-6; 51:4-5; 56:6-7; 60:1-3; 66:23), but a savior of the nations! Genesis 3:15 is fulfilled, as well as Gen. 12:3!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "write on his hand, 'Belonging to the Lord'" This seems to reflect the ANE
custom of slaves being tattooed with the name of their owner. This would be similar imagery to God marking His followers' foreheads.

- Paul, in Gal. 6:17, mentions a "brand/mark of Jesus"

- God marks His faithful followers who believe in Jesus on their hand or forehead in Rev. 7:3

- Satan mimics this in Rev. 13:16; 14:9; 20:4

The interpretive question is, "Does this line of poetry match v. 21a, "remember" (Qal

The bases for this complete blotting out of our transgressions are
